body.statement: For every \(v\in\mathbb B_*\), \(h_{\mathcal T}(v)=\sum_z\int(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z})\,dv_z+\sum_z\{V_{1,z}(v_z;u)+V_{0,z}(-v_z;u)\}\). For the grid problem, writing \(w_j=\int\phi_{j,h}\,dv_z\) and \(\bar u_j=[u_{a,z}(r_j)-Mh^\beta]_+\), strong duality gives \(\sup_{x:0\le x_j\le\bar u_j,\,0\le x_{j+1}-x_j\le Lh}\sum_jw_jx_j=\min_{d_h=(\lambda^+,\lambda^-,g,d)\in\mathcal D_h(w,\bar u)}\{\sum_j\bar u_j\lambda_j^+ +Lh\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}g_j\}\). The primal and dual are a path min-cost transshipment pair, and their equality is a finite certificate for each support direction.
body.justification: A directionwise support identity and primal-dual flow certificate make the infinite-dimensional set auditable rather than merely definitional.
body.gap: Kim's Theorem 1 uses transport duality for fixed-marginal DTE bounds, and Chiang et al.'s Theorem 1 projects a sieve confidence region by generic linear programs; neither yields the dropout-capacity path dual.
body.consumer: Software can return a primal curve and a dual certificate for every clinical leaf or plotted support direction.
